cover.kicker: Printable sub-folder stations for calm story writing
cover.headline: Substitute Teacher Story Station Pack
cover.subhead: A ready-to-use set of story station routines, quiet extension cards, and handoff notes for ages 7-11 in classrooms, homeschool co-ops, tutoring centers, and substitute folders.
included: One-page substitute guide for quick planning
Eight early finisher cards for quiet writing choices
Six share prompts for gentle discussion
Simple setup notes for desks, tables, or floor spots
Printable-only directions with no digital tools required
Flexible timing for short blocks or full rotations
Teacher handoff notes focused on completed materials
Calm routines that work without grading pressure

beforeTheDay: Print one routine page for each station you plan to use.
Print enough early finisher cards for quiet choice work.
Place pencils, blank paper, and the selected station pages in one folder.
Choose three to five stations based on the time available.
Leave a simple note telling students that every story world is invented.
morningSetup: Set station pages where students can reach them without extra explanation.
Put blank paper beside each station page.
Post or read the station order before students begin.
Keep early finisher cards in a separate quiet-choice stack.
Use a visible timer if the group already follows timed rotations.
duringStations: Read the first direction aloud, then let students work independently or with a partner.
Remind students to write about invented characters and places only.
Encourage short, complete ideas instead of perfect spelling.
Rotate when the group is ready, or let students finish one station deeply.
Use early finisher cards for students who complete a station before the group moves on.
endOfDay: Ask students to place finished pages in the class work stack or take-home folder.
Collect unused station pages so the teacher can reuse them.
Circle any station that students especially enjoyed.
Note whether the group completed all planned rotations or only part of the set.
Leave early finisher cards in the substitute folder for future use.
handoff: Students completed printable story station work from invented-world prompts.
No digital tools, personal details, or online sharing were used.
The strongest participation appeared during the station choices marked on the pages.
Unused pages and quiet-choice cards are returned to the folder.

stationRoutines.name: Map the Tiny Kingdom
stationRoutines.bestFor: A calm first station when students need a clear starting point
steps: Draw a small invented kingdom with three places: a gate, a workshop, and a quiet garden.
Label each place with one detail that could start a story.
Choose one place and write what a friendly character notices there.
Add one kind problem the character can solve before leaving the kingdom.

stationRoutines.name: Message from Moonberry Mail
stationRoutines.bestFor: Pairs or independent writers who enjoy letter-style prompts
steps: Imagine a mail cart arrives from a town called Moonberry Hollow.
Write the first three sentences of the message inside the envelope.
Decide what helpful errand the message asks the reader to complete.
Write a short reply explaining the first step of the plan.

stationRoutines.name: Three Object Story Tray
stationRoutines.bestFor: Students who benefit from concrete choices before drafting
steps: Pick three invented objects: a glowing button, a silver seed, and a paper compass.
Choose which object a character finds first.
Write how the object changes the character's plan for the day.
End with the character using one object to help a neighbor in the story world.

stationRoutines.name: Quiet Quest Countdown
stationRoutines.bestFor: Short blocks, tutoring sessions, or a final station before cleanup
steps: Fold a page into four boxes and number them one through four.
In box one, sketch a peaceful invented place.
In boxes two and three, write two steps a character takes to complete a small quest.
In box four, write one sentence showing how the place is better at the end.

stationRoutines.name: Story Helper Circle
stationRoutines.bestFor: Small groups that need a structured way to build one shared idea
steps: Each student writes one invented setting on a scrap of paper.
Choose one setting and place it in the center of the group.
Each student adds one friendly helper, tool, or clue for that setting.
Independently write a short scene using the shared setting and one added idea.

earlyFinisherCards.title: New Door Detail
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Add a door, archway, or path to your story world and write what makes it interesting.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Helper's Pocket
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Draw three safe objects a friendly helper carries, then write how one object is useful.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Better Ending
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Write a second ending where the character solves the problem in a quieter or kinder way.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Five-Sense Place
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Choose one invented place from your page and add one sight, sound, smell, texture, and taste.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Tiny Problem Swap
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Replace your story problem with a small mix-up, missing object, or confusing clue.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Friendly Dialogue
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Write four lines of conversation between two invented characters who are making a plan.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Quest List
earlyFinisherCards.direction: List three steps your character could take next, then circle the step that would make the best scene.

earlyFinisherCards.title: Title Test
earlyFinisherCards.direction: Write three possible titles for your story and underline the one that gives the clearest clue.

sharePrompts: Read one sentence that shows where your story takes place.
Share one invented object and explain why it matters.
Tell the group one kind choice your character made.
Name one detail you added after your first draft.
Share a title and explain which story clue it gives.
Tell one next scene you could write if you had more time.
